notes:
The RX reference model from the "assumptions" was not in the prompt, so I inferred it. Assumptions: H = N/2 (integer division). T0 is the first edge where i_rxd samples 0 while the model is idle, and s(t) is i_rxd sampled at edge t. A glitch is s(T0+H)=1. The model is idle again at M+1. V = M+2. Reset clears the model. The second assertion for CHK-009 (a_CHK_009_b) has no hit counter of its own, so it adds to fails_CHK_009 only. It also has the same load-edge limitation: a held byte taken at V with a new load is counted as a load. If the DUT's real T0, H or re-arm rules differ from these, the model's V edges will be off and the checks will mismatch.

I did not compile or simulate this in Verilator. One ordering problem: `mdl_m1_d2` is used in an assign before its declaration, so move its declaration above that assign.
